main_text.p: vero, ait Polybius, Apollonius Sicyonius assurgens sic difleruit: pecuniam ab Eumene oblatam magnitudine sui dignam sanè esse, quæ donetur Achæis: sed si animum & scopum donantis consideres, rem esse cum turpissimam tum iniquissimam. Τῶν [?] νόμων κα[?]λυόντων, ait, μηδένα μήτε ἰδιωτῶν, μήτε τ̃ ἀρχόντων ἀπ̓ βασιλέως δώ[?]ρα λαμβάνειν, [?]μηδ' ὁποῖαν οὖν ἀποφαίνειν, [?]πάντων εἶναι ἀπογεμώτερον. Atque his congrua alia plura subtexuit, oftendens, si accepta fuerit pecunia regia, oportere accipientes velut efcâ devoratâ captos, aut mercede auctoratos neceflariò è duobus alterum committere, nimirum aut regis commoda, quæ naturâ pugnant cum commodis liberarum civitatum, bono patriæ poftponere, aut si faciant fecus, in crimen ingratitudinis fe conjicere, opponentes fe defideriis ejus, cujus erunt mercenarii. Denique ea vis orationis iftius fuit, ut plurimi Eumenem odio [?]tius quàm favore dignum esse ob hoc [?]nfilium ejus judicarent. Et quam-publicè amicitia ejus rejecta non fit, largi-

page.notes: Greek lines are low-confidence: the words marked [?] are best readings and the Greek should be checked against the scan. The left edge carries cut-off fragments of text (for example "u", "ıc ın", "II", "ut ıu") that are too truncated to read; they were not transcribed. The lines beginning "tius quàm" and "nfilium" are cut at the left edge, so their first letters are uncertain. The word "afliurgens" as printed was read as "assurgens" with long s. The line "ptius" and the "nfilium" fragment are at the page edge and may be incomplete.
